clue.text: One stands under bridge-healthy job!

parts.note: healthy means sound, as in sound in body and mind
a job is a post, a position of employment

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fit worker's role propping up a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is a violin's: the small wooden peg inside the body sits beneath it and carries sound to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: On a violin, a slender dowel stands inside the body directly below the bridge, supporting it and transmitting vibration.

clue.text: Bond shows round hat, askew

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: askew means set crookedly, so the letters of the word are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A secret agent turns up wearing a round hat cocked to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy, but it is a binding promise. 'askew' scrambles HAT to ATH, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn promise binds the speaker, so it is a solemn pledge or bond.

clue.text: Foster taking hours in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carer takes some hours off at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is the anagram signal (re-sort): HOURS and IN are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster growth or a child is to nurture and feed it.

clue.text: Coaster's cargo put between road-rail and fire-wood

definitions.text: Coaster's cargo put between road-rail and fire-wood

parts.words: Coaster's cargo put between road-rail and fire-wood
parts.note: in Masefield's poem Cargoes the dirty British coaster carries a list of goods, and this metal in ingots comes between road-rails and firewood

explanation.surface: A stevedore stows a small ship's load between rails and logs.
explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield's poem 'Cargoes' lists the coaster's cargo: Tyne coal, road-rails, pig-lead, firewood, iron-ware and cheap tin trays.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead cast in oblong ingots from the smelter is a typical bulk freight for a small coastal ship, as in Masefield's list.

clue.text: Exclusive walking-on part

definitions.meaning: exclusive in the sense of only, belonging to one alone
the underside of the foot or shoe, the part one walks on

explanation.walkthrough: 'walking-on part' sounds like a minor stage role but means the bottom of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning only or single in one sense, and the underside of the foot in the other.

clue.text: Person I blamed wrongly for things difficult to assess

indicators.note: wrongly signals that the letters are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone I unfairly blamed was struggling with matters hard to judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' shuffles PERSON, I and BLAMED into the thirteen-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Factors whose effect cannot be measured or weighed are by nature hard to evaluate.

clue.text: This meeting between banks produces many rows

definitions.text: This meeting between banks produces many rows

parts.words: This meeting between banks produces many rows
parts.note: a meeting held on a river between its banks where rowing crews race, so there is much rowing, not quarrelling

explanation.surface: A summit between rival financial institutions generates endless arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks are river banks, not lenders, and rows are bouts of rowing, not quarrels: the famous rowing event on the Thames in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual rowing races on the Thames at an Oxfordshire town are a meeting on the river with many boats rowing.

clue.text: There is no bread at the end of his round

definitions.text: There is no bread at the end of his round

parts.words: There is no bread at the end of his round
parts.note: bread is slang for money, and a round is a round of a sport played on a course; this player gets no prize money

explanation.surface: A baker's delivery driver finds no loaves left by the end of his route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for cash and 'round' is a round on the links: a player who competes without being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional on the links plays for no money, so there are no winnings after his round.

clue.text: Letter opener?

parts.note: not a paper knife but the person who opens a letter because it is meant for them

explanation.walkthrough: A letter opener is usually a knife; here it is the person the letter is sent to.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom mail is sent is the one entitled to open it.

clue.text: Tricky dealer?

parts.note: a dealer at the card table who cheats, using tricks

explanation.walkthrough: 'dealer' suggests trade; here it is the one dealing cards, dishonestly, with 'tricky' nodding to tricks in card games.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat who swindles at card games is a dishonest dealer of hands.

clue.text: Doctor to work a little

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A physician heading off to his job for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount of liquid, as in just a spot, is a small quantity.

clue.text: Tape of Ovid with English construction

indicators.note: construction means building something new from parts, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A recording of the Roman poet Ovid with an English building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' rebuilds OVID plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette recording of moving pictures is a recording on tape.

clue.text: Mid-off takes the field with a jumper

indicators.note: mid asks for the middle letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A cricketer fielding at mid-off moves into the outfield with a woolly pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here 'Mid' takes the centre letter of 'off'. 'a jumper' looks like a sweater but is a leaping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The parasitic insect is famous for leaping huge distances relative to its size.

clue.text: No honours, presumably, for the Browning girl

definitions.text: No honours, presumably, for the Browning girl

parts.words: No honours, presumably, for the Browning girl
parts.note: a degree without honours is a pass degree, and Browning wrote a verse drama about a girl who passes

explanation.surface: A university examiner refuses a first-class result to a student named Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning's dramatic poem is 'Pippa Passes'; a pass degree is one awarded without honours.
explanation.definitionFit: The silk-mill girl of Asolo is the heroine of Robert Browning's dramatic poem, whose title says she passes.

clue.text: Female's first defeat as Eliot's mill-turner

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: A woman's first loss is pictured as George Eliot's tragic heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot wrote 'The Mill on the Floss'; the river drives the mill's wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: In George Eliot's novel the mill stands on this river, whose current turns its wheel.

clue.text: Does that describe Bloody Hugh, would you say?

definitions.text: Does that describe Bloody Hugh, would you say?

parts.words: Does that describe Bloody Hugh, would you say?
parts.note: spoken, the name Hugh sounds like hue, so a bloody hue is a colour like blood

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a violent man called Hugh deserves his nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would you say' tells you to hear 'Hugh' as 'hue': a blood-coloured hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tinged the colour of blood has a red hue.

clue.text: Act includes ballad, slowed up

indicators.note: includes means one word takes another inside it

parts.note: an act is a deed
a lay is a narrative song or ballad

explanation.surface: A stage act featuring a ballad drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts LAY inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held back or made late has been slowed in its progress.

clue.text: Turbulent priest died like a tiger

indicators.note: turbulent means wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A troublesome cleric died a death as violent as a tiger's attack.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Henry II's 'turbulent priest', Becket; 'Turbulent' scrambles PRIEST to STRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger's coat is marked with dark stripes.

clue.text: But, at sea, it is not a tramp

definitions.text: But, at sea, it is not a tramp

parts.words: But, at sea, it is not a tramp
parts.note: on land the word names a vagrant, but at sea it is a fishing boat, not a tramp steamer

explanation.surface: A remark that a sailor is different from a vagabond.
explanation.walkthrough: On land the word means a vagrant, a tramp; at sea it is a fishing boat with drift nets, as opposed to a tramp steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing vessel using drift nets is not a cargo tramp, though on shore the word means a wanderer.

clue.text: Pray, begin breakfast with cheese-spread

indicators.note: begin asks for the first letter of the following word
spread means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Say grace, then start the morning meal with cheese spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheese-spread' looks like a food; 'spread' scrambles CHEESE after the B from 'begin breakfast'.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore or entreat earnestly is to pray in the old sense.

clue.text: Coarse fellows working on a diamond?

definitions.meaning: low, vulgar men, base meaning crude
players stationed at the bases of a baseball diamond

explanation.walkthrough: A diamond is a baseball infield, not a gem; American players at first, second and third base.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means vulgar people; as one it names infield players at baseball's bases.

clue.text: Qualified for retirement in Mediterranean island

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the word for qualified is read backwards

parts.note: able means qualified or competent

explanation.surface: Someone eligible to retire settles on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' turns ABLE backwards; fitting, as Napoleon was retired to this island.
explanation.definitionFit: The island off Tuscany where Napoleon spent his first exile lies in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Get up about noon and bathe

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to get up is to rise

explanation.surface: A lie-in: rise around midday and have a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash lightly in water is to bathe or rinse off.

clue.text: Musical shock?

definitions.meaning: the 1960s rock stage show of the hippie era
a shock is a thick mass of ... on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests surprise, but a shock of hair is a thick tousled mop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the 1967 tribal rock stage show and the mop of strands on the head.

clue.text: Solid fuel that will pass in church

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OK, said of something acceptable that will do or pass muster

explanation.surface: A heating fuel that will do inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OK inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: The residue of coal after baking is a smokeless solid fuel.

clue.text: Storm-cone for a single occasion

indicators.note: storm suggests violent disturbance, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A storm cone is hoisted just one time to warn ships.
explanation.walkthrough: A storm cone is a signal hoisted to warn of gales; here 'Storm' scrambles CONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Done only one time, on one solitary occasion.

clue.text: Comedian, at ten, in variety has to remove all dirty material

indicators.note: variety means many different forms, so the letters are put in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A comic on the variety stage at ten must clean up his blue act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' suggests the music-hall stage; 'in variety' scrambles COMEDIAN, AT, TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse of pollution or radioactive matter is to strip away harmful contaminants.

clue.text: The German double-pistol

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
a ringer is a dead ringer, someone's double or lookalike

explanation.surface: A German man has two guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double-pistol' looks like a twin-barrelled weapon; the hyphen joins two parts with separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pocket handgun named after its Philadelphia maker, Henry Deringer.
